title: Verbs that use être
goal: Say where you went, when you left and arrived, and where you were born, using the passé composé with être.

items.en: passé composé with être (movement and change verbs)

drills.en: On Friday we left at 6 p.m.
drills.explain: partir uses être: nous sommes partis.

drills.prompt: How do you say “He went to Ottawa”?
drills.explain: aller uses être, and its participle is allé.
venir uses être: tu es venu.
arriver uses être; with ils, the participle takes -s: arrivés.

items.note: A woman writes: Je suis allée. It sounds the same.

blocks.title: Monday morning, again
blocks.context: Karim, from Casablanca, spent his weekend in Québec City. Camille grew up there.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Karim ! Tu es allé à Québec en fin de semaine, non ?
lines.en: Karim! You went to Québec City on the weekend, didn't you?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Oui ! Je suis parti vendredi soir avec mon frère. On a pris le train à la gare Centrale et nous sommes arrivés à 22 h.
lines.en: Yes! I left on Friday evening with my brother. We took the train at Central Station and we arrived at 10 p.m.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Et qu'est-ce que vous avez visité ?

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Samedi, nous sommes montés au Château Frontenac par le funiculaire. Ensuite, on est descendus dans le Petit Champlain à pied. Mon frère est tombé dans l'escalier Casse-Cou !
lines.en: On Saturday we went up to the Château Frontenac by the funicular. Then we walked down into Petit Champlain. My brother fell on the Breakneck Stairs!

lines.speaker: Karim
lines.fr: Oui, oui. Après, on a pris le traversier pour Lévis : la vue est magnifique. Nous sommes restés deux jours et nous sommes rentrés dimanche soir.
lines.en: Yes, yes. Afterwards we took the ferry to Lévis: the view is amazing. We stayed two days and came back on Sunday evening.

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Ah, j'adore Québec. Je suis née là-bas, tu sais. Mes parents sont venus à Montréal quand j'avais dix ans.
lines.en: Ah, I love Québec City. I was born there, you know. My parents came to Montréal when I was ten.

blocks.body: Look at the helper verb. [[On a pris le train]] uses **avoir**, but [[je suis parti]], [[nous sommes arrivés]], [[il est tombé]] use **être**. Why? That is today's lesson.

blocks.prompt: How long did Karim stay in Québec City?
blocks.explain: [[Nous sommes restés deux jours]]: rester = to stay.

blocks.title: A small group of verbs uses être
blocks.body:
Most verbs form the passé composé with **avoir**. But about **17 verbs** use **être** instead. Almost all of them describe a **movement from one place to another** or a **change of state** (being born, dying, becoming).

The structure is the same, with [[je suis, tu es, il est…]] in place of [[j'ai, tu as, il a…]]:

- [[Je suis allé à Québec.]] I went to Québec City.
- [[Nous sommes arrivés à 22 h.]] We arrived at 10 p.m.

One more thing: with être, the participle **agrees with the subject**, like an adjective: [[elle est allée]], [[nous sommes allés]]. You will practise this in the next lesson; for now, notice the extra **-e** and **-s**.

blocks.title: The house of être
head: Pair
Infinitives
Participles
rows: come back / go back / return home
blocks.note: Picture a **house**: you **arrive** at the door, **go in**, **go up** the stairs, **go down**, **stay** inside, **fall** down the stairs, **go out**, **leave**… and people are **born** and **die** there.

blocks.title: Aller in the passé composé
head: être
participle
blocks.note: All these forms of [[allé]] sound exactly the same. The difference is only in writing. When [[on]] means *we*, you will also see [[on est allés]] (agreement with the real people); both are accepted.

blocks.title: DR MRS VANDERTRAMP
blocks.body:
Many English-speaking learners use this acronym: each letter is one être verb.

**D**evenir, **R**evenir, **M**onter, **R**ester, **S**ortir, **V**enir, **A**ller, **N**aître, **D**escendre, **E**ntrer, **R**entrer, **T**omber, **R**etourner, **A**rriver, **M**ourir, **P**artir.

Use whichever memory trick works for you: the house or the acronym. Also remember [[passer]] in the sense of *to pass by*: [[Je suis passé par Trois-Rivières.]]

- [[J'ai allé]] → [[Je suis allé]]. This is the classic mistake; aller always uses être.
- [[Je suis aller]] → [[Je suis allé]]: the participle, not the infinitive.
- **I was born:** [[Je suis né en 1992]]. It looks like *I am born*, but it is the passé composé of naître. Not [[J'ai né]].
- **Rester ≠ to rest.** [[Je suis resté à la maison]] = I stayed home. To rest is [[se reposer]].
- **Not every movement verb uses être:** [[marcher]] (walk), [[voyager]], [[courir]] (run) and [[prendre le train]] use avoir: [[J'ai voyagé]], [[On a marché]].

blocks.title: à Québec or au Québec?
blocks.body:
- [[à Québec]] = in **Québec City** (a city: à).
- [[au Québec]] = in the **province** of Québec (a masculine place name: au).

So: [[Je suis allé à Québec]] = I went to Québec City; [[Je suis arrivé au Québec en 2021]] = I arrived in Québec (the province) in 2021.

As in Unit 1, you will hear [[J'ai été à Québec]] in casual Québec speech for *I went to Québec City*. It is informal: understand it, but in writing and exams, use [[Je suis allé]]. And the ferry between Québec and Lévis is [[le traversier]], the usual word in Québec.

lines.tip: suis allé: swee-za-lé, with a z link.
sont arrivés: son-ta-ri-vé, with a t link.

blocks.fr: Ils sont arrivés à Ottawa ce matin.
blocks.en: They arrived in Ottawa this morning.
blocks.prompt: Which helper verb did you hear?
blocks.explain: [[sont]] with an *s* sound, then a *t* link: [[sont‿arrivés]]. [[ont]] would start with a *z* link: [[ils‿ont]].

blocks.fr: Tu es venue en train ou en autobus ?
blocks.en: Did you come by train or by bus?
blocks.prompt: What does the speaker want to know?
blocks.explain: [[Tu es venue]] = you came (venir, past). [[en train ou en autobus]] = by train or by bus.

blocks.prompt: Tell a colleague about a short trip you took (real or imagined): where you went, when you left, how you got there, when you arrived, how long you stayed and when you came back.
checklist: je suis parti / partie + day or time
Transport with avoir: j'ai pris le train / l'autobus

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Le mois dernier, je suis allée à Ottawa avec une amie. Nous sommes parties samedi matin. On a pris l'autobus et nous sommes arrivées à midi. Nous sommes restées deux jours et nous sommes rentrées dimanche soir. J'ai adoré !
models.en: (A woman speaking.) Last month I went to Ottawa with a friend. We left on Saturday morning. We took the bus and arrived at noon. We stayed two days and came back on Sunday evening. I loved it!

blocks.prompt: Fill in a short “About me” for the company newsletter: where and when you were born, when you arrived in Canada (or in your city), and one trip you took recently.
checklist: je suis né / née à… en…
je suis arrivé / arrivée au Canada en…
One trip with je suis allé / allée
One verb with avoir for contrast

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Je m'appelle Raj. Je suis né à Pune, en Inde, en 1994. Je suis arrivé au Canada il y a trois ans. L'été dernier, je suis allé aux chutes Niagara avec ma femme. Nous avons pris beaucoup de photos !
models.en: My name is Raj. I was born in Pune, in India, in 1994. I arrived in Canada three years ago. Last summer I went to Niagara Falls with my wife. We took lots of photos!

summary:
- Recognize the **être** verbs: movement and change ([[aller, venir, partir, arriver, rester, naître…]])
- Say [[je suis allé à Québec]], [[nous sommes arrivés à 22 h]], [[je suis né à…]]
- Choose **être** or **avoir** in the same story
- Use [[à Québec]] (city) and [[au Québec]] (province)
